procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory (prerequisite) before applying for a certificate of origin for India.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The exporter applies for a certificate of origin for India through the e-service: logs in to the ministry e-services portal, chooses the Certificate of Origin for India service, fills in the application form, uploads the required documents, submits the application, and receives approval or a return with comments to correct, then prints the approved certificate.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 (band: invoice value up to AED 100000).

The competent authority issues the certificate of origin, which is valid for 12 months from the date of issue, covers only one import, and should be issued prior to, at, or within five working days of the date of exportation; it may be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 (Remarks).

The issuing authority requires the application to include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product, and each item must qualify separately in its own right; it may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and conducting a factory visit.

The exporter ensures that the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control, with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar; if the invoice is issued by a third party, the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information under CAROTAR 2020 including which origin criterion is claimed, keeps supporting documents for at least five years from filing, and must answer a customs request within ten working days.

The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years starting from the end of the year of the date of its issue; any failure to consent to a verification visit shall be grounds for a denial of preferential benefits.

caveats.note: The '+' in the rule 'CTSH + VA 45%' is interpreted as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+'.
The operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
The duty estimate is on the shipment value given; India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
Direct labour cost and direct overhead cost are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The 40% value-added letter is a registration condition only; it is NOT the CEPA product-specific rule test, which is set per tariff line.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).
The certificate fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
